variations.name: Nitrogen-fixing microbes / biological nitrogen fixation
variations.description: Engineered or naturally-selected bacteria applied to seeds or roots pull nitrogen from the air and feed it to non-legume crops like corn and wheat, replacing 20-50 lbs/acre of synthetic nitrogen and cutting the N2O and CO2 footprint of fertilizer manufacture and field loss.
variations.white_space: Despite ~$1B cumulative VC, no product reliably replaces more than ~25% of nitrogen; biological N is dosage-limited by microbe colonization and oxygen sensitivity of nitrogenase, and farmers won't pay for an input they must still backstop with urea. Opening: strains that fix N even under high soil-nitrate conditions (the ammonia 'switch-off' problem) and verifiable yield-or-money-back guarantees to overcome trust gap.

companies.name: Pivot Bio
companies.what: Gene-edits soil microbes (e.g. Kosakonia, Klebsiella) so they keep fixing nitrogen even when fertilizer is present; on-seed PROVEN line for corn, sorghum, spring wheat.
companies.signal: $430M Series D (DCVC, Temasek) bringing total to ~$1B+; deployed on millions of acres; cut research footprint by exiting Berkeley and consolidating to St. Louis (2025).

companies.name: Kula Bio
companies.what: Uses Xanthobacter autotrophicus charged with an energy reserve, sold as shelf-stable soluble powders (Kula-NSP, Kula-NextSP) delivered to the root zone.
companies.signal: Raised >$70M; commercial launch of shelf-stable powder line; claims up to 65% greater fixation efficiency vs conventional diazotrophs.

companies.name: Azotic Technologies
companies.what: Envita product uses Gluconacetobacter diazotrophicus, an endophyte that colonizes inside plant cells across many crops to fix atmospheric nitrogen.
companies.signal: 7 years of US sales growth, millions of acres treated; 3rd most-recognized biological brand in North America per company; new CEO appointed June 2025 to accelerate global commercialization.

companies.name: Corteva Agriscience (Utrisha N)
companies.what: Foliar biostimulant using a licensed strain of Methylobacterium symbioticum (SB23) that colonizes leaves and fixes airborne nitrogen into ammonium inside the plant.
companies.signal: Globally registered and sold by a major agrochem incumbent; delivers ~30 kg N/ha per season; backed by Corteva's distribution scale.

companies.name: Andes
companies.what: Microprime seed-treatment combines seeds with a microbe library that colonizes the root structure to boost biological nitrogen fixation; also pursuing soil carbon removal.
companies.signal: $15M Series A co-led by Leaps by Bayer and Cavallo Ventures (Wilbur-Ellis) in early 2025; first-gen corn product targets 30-50 lbs N/acre.

companies.name: Ginkgo Bioworks (Joyn Bio legacy, Bayer alliance)
companies.what: Applies AI-driven cell programming to engineer next-gen nitrogen-fixing microbes for Bayer, building on assets of the former Joyn Bio JV folded into Ginkgo in 2022.
companies.signal: Bayer-Ginkgo partnership renewed/extended Nov 2025 to develop field-ready N-fixing biologicals with improved efficacy, stability and cost.

companies.name: BioConsortia
companies.what: Uses directed-selection of microbial communities to develop nitrogen-fixing strains for cereal crops; partnered with fertilizer major Mosaic on commercialization.
companies.signal: Mosaic-BioConsortia collaboration announced to bring nitrogen-fixing microbial products to market; backs lab-to-field strain discovery platform.

companies.name: Switch Bioworks
companies.what: Engineers microbes that first establish on plant roots, then 'switch on' nitrogen fertilizer production — designed to solve colonization-vs-fixation tradeoff.
companies.signal: Early-stage; profiled Nov 2025 as a novel approach to the root-colonization bottleneck in microbial N.

variations.name: Enhanced-efficiency fertilizers, coatings & nitrification/urease inhibitors
variations.description: Polymer coatings, urease inhibitors (e.g. NBPT) and nitrification inhibitors (e.g. pronitridine, DMPP) slow the conversion of fertilizer nitrogen into leachable nitrate and volatile ammonia, keeping more N in the root zone and directly suppressing N2O emissions — the single largest near-term lever on fertilizer climate impact.

companies.name: Koch Agronomic Services (Koch Industries)
companies.what: Market-leading inhibitor portfolio: AGROTAIN (NBPT urease inhibitor), CENTURO/CENTURO A-PRO (pronitridine nitrification inhibitor for anhydrous ammonia/UAN), ANVOL, and SUPERU dual-inhibitor stabilized urea.
companies.signal: 25+ years of NBPT field data on millions of acres; CENTURO A-PRO offers 3x active-ingredient concentration at lower use rate; EPA-approved pronitridine technology.

companies.name: Nutrien (ESN)
companies.what: ESN (Environmentally Smart Nitrogen) is a polymer-coated controlled-release urea; Nutrien also distributes inhibitor-treated products through its retail network.
companies.signal: Record upstream fertilizer sales volumes in 9 months of 2025; ESN is a flagship controlled-release product in the world's largest ag-retail network.

companies.name: Yara International
companies.what: Global nitrogen major offering nitrate-based and inhibitor-enhanced fertilizers (e.g. YaraVera/YaraBela lines) plus DMPP-type nitrification inhibitor products to lower N losses.
companies.signal: One of the world's largest nitrogen fertilizer producers; positions enhanced-efficiency and low-carbon fertilizer as core decarbonization strategy.

companies.name: Verdesian Life Sciences
companies.what: Specialty nutrient-use-efficiency additives including NutriSphere-N (urease/nitrification management polymer) and a portfolio of biostimulant and fertilizer-coating chemistries.
companies.signal: Established specialty player focused exclusively on nutrient-efficiency and biological additives; broad distribution across US row crops.

companies.name: Corteva Agriscience (Instinct / N-Serve)
companies.what: Sells the nitrapyrin-based nitrification inhibitors N-Serve (for anhydrous ammonia) and Instinct (for UAN/manure), among the longest-running EEF chemistries in the US.
companies.signal: Nitrapyrin franchise long established in US corn; backed by Corteva's crop-protection distribution and field-trial network.

variations.name: Green, distributed & on-farm ammonia / nitrogen production (ag-side)
variations.description: Modular, renewable-powered electrolysis-plus-Haber-Bosch (or novel electrochemical) units make ammonia or nitrate fertilizer at or near the farm from air, water and clean electricity, eliminating the fossil-gas feedstock that gives synthetic nitrogen most of its CO2 footprint and cutting import/logistics dependence.
variations.white_space: Economics are brutal at small scale: distributed green ammonia only pencils where renewable power is cheap and fertilizer imports are expensive (sub-Saharan Africa, remote Midwest, Brazil). Electrochemical 'ammonia without Haber-Bosch' remains pilot-stage on energy efficiency. Opening: hybrid models that co-locate with existing ethanol/renewable plants (Tsubame-Atvos) or convert almond/biomass waste to fertilizer (Nitricity), sidestepping pure-play electrolysis cost.

companies.name: Talus Renewables
companies.what: Modular, containerized zero-carbon green ammonia systems (TalusOne) for on-site/regional fertilizer; first US commercial unit with farmer co-op Landus in Iowa.
companies.signal: Opened first-of-a-kind commercial distributed green ammonia facility with Landus (Iowa); farmers able to use green anhydrous ammonia from spring 2025.

companies.name: Nitricity
companies.what: Uses renewable electricity and a plasma/electrochemical process plus recycled almond-shell biomass to make 'Ash Tea,' a liquid organic nitrogen fertilizer at point-of-use.
companies.signal: $50M Series B (Sept 2025; World Fund, Khosla, Chipotle's Cultivate Next); first commercial plant in Delhi, CA breaking ground, output sold out through 2028; claims up to 92% emissions cut.

companies.name: Atlas Agro
companies.what: Builds industrial-scale green nitrogen fertilizer plants producing green hydrogen, ammonia and ammonium nitrate from renewables; Richland WA (US) and Uberaba (Brazil) projects.
companies.signal: Commenced engineering on first Brazil plant; selected KBR green ammonia tech; signed low-carbon fertilizer supply agreement with Tereos; FID expected ~2025, production ~2027-28.

companies.name: Tsubame BHB
companies.what: Japanese firm with a low-temperature/low-pressure catalytic process enabling small-scale on-site ammonia synthesis in distributed locations.
companies.signal: Raised ¥5.3B Series C; signed LOI with Atvos (Brazil) for a 20,000 t/yr renewable-powered aqueous ammonia plant co-located with an ethanol facility to replace fossil fertilizers.

companies.name: FuelPositive
companies.what: Decentralized on-farm green ammonia systems (FP300, ~300 kg ammonia/day) for Canadian farmers, running on hydroelectric grid power.
companies.signal: Partnered with Stantec on Canada's first farmer-owned green ammonia system; publicly traded (TSXV); FP300 targets farms of hundreds-to-thousands of acres.

companies.name: Nitricity / Atmonia
companies.what: Atmonia (Iceland) is developing an electrochemical catalyst to make ammonia directly from air and water at ambient conditions, bypassing Haber-Bosch.
companies.signal: Partnered with Fujitsu on materials-informatics catalyst discovery; remains lab/pilot stage on energy efficiency.

variations.name: Microbial biostimulants, biofertilizers & mycorrhizae
variations.description: Living microbes — plant-growth-promoting rhizobacteria, mycorrhizal fungi, and bacterial 'microbiome activators' — applied to seed, soil or foliage improve nutrient uptake and stress tolerance so crops need less synthetic N and P, while mycorrhizae can also store soil carbon.
variations.white_space: Funding to the category fell ~86% from its 2023 peak; efficacy is highly variable across soils and seasons, and many products are sold on agronomic 'activation' claims that are hard to verify, eroding farmer trust. Opening: outcome-based pricing (paying growers to cut fertilizer) and pairing biostimulants with carbon-credit revenue (mycorrhizae) to monetize beyond yield.

companies.name: Sound Agriculture
companies.what: SOURCE is a small-molecule 'microbiome activator' that stimulates native soil microbes to free up nitrogen and phosphorus; BLUEPRINT delivers arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi.
companies.signal: ~$195M raised over 8 rounds; $25M Series D extension (Dec 2024, BMO/S2G, Leaps by Bayer, Syngenta Ventures); now pays growers to replace N and P.

companies.name: Groundwork BioAg
companies.what: Manufactures Rootella mycorrhizal inoculants at scale for broad-acre crops, improving nutrient/water uptake and enabling soil-carbon storage.
companies.signal: ~$29M raised over 3 rounds; latest Series C+ (Nov 2025); partnered with Indigo Ag to combine mycorrhizae with microbial endophytes.

companies.name: Indigo Ag
companies.what: Microbial seed treatments (Biotrinsic line) using endophytes to boost yield and stress tolerance; also runs a carbon program; partnered on mycorrhizae with Groundwork BioAg.
companies.signal: Raised a $270M round in 2023 (one of the largest biologicals deals); large microbial endophyte collection and broad US commercial footprint.

companies.name: Loam Bio
companies.what: Microbial seed inoculum (CarbonBuilder) using fungi to increase stable soil-carbon storage; SecondCrop monetizes soil-carbon credits for farmers.
companies.signal: A$105M (~$73M) Series B co-led by Lowercarbon Capital and Wollemi; ~$120M total; commercially launched in Australia.

companies.name: Biobest
companies.what: Belgian biologicals major spanning biocontrol and biostimulants/beneficial microbes; a consolidating buyer in the sector.
companies.signal: Raised ~$391M in 2023, one of the two mega-rounds that drove the category's funding peak; broad European/global commercial scale.

companies.name: Corteva Agriscience
companies.what: Major agrochem incumbent that has built/acquired a biologicals portfolio (biostimulants and microbial nutrient-efficiency products such as Utrisha N).
companies.signal: Publicly committed to scaling biologicals as a growth segment; global distribution and field-development infrastructure.

variations.name: Biopesticides, biocontrol & RNAi crop protection
variations.description: Naturally-derived or precision tools — microbial biopesticides, insect pheromones, and sprayable RNA interference that silences a specific pest gene — replace broad-spectrum synthetic chemistry, reducing the manufacturing and field emissions and ecological harm of conventional pesticides while preserving yield.
variations.white_space: RNAi sprays are at most demonstration-stage commercially (one registered foliar product), constrained by RNA stability, delivery cost, and slow EPA pathways; pheromones only recently became cheap enough for row crops. Opening: low-cost biomanufacturing (Provivi-style biocatalysis) and platform RNAi to compress the cost-per-acre that has blocked broad-acre adoption.

companies.name: GreenLight Biosciences
companies.what: Cell-free biomanufacturing of double-stranded RNA for sprayable RNAi pesticides; Calantha (ledprona) is the first EPA-registered foliar RNA crop-protection product, targeting Colorado potato beetle.
companies.signal: Survived a failed SPAC and 2023 take-private by Fall Line Capital (~$45.5M); €35M EIB loan (Feb 2025) + $25M Series C extension; pipeline of ~10 EU products; aims to register 7 ag products by end-2026.

companies.name: Provivi
companies.what: Uses biocatalysis/fermentation to make insect mating-disruption pheromones cheaply enough for row crops (corn, rice, soy); Pheron line targets fall armyworm and stem borers.
companies.signal: Raised >$230M (Gates Foundation, BASF VC, Temasek); in 2025 signed 5 regional partnerships (UPL, Koppert do Brasil, AgNova, Andermatt, Susbin) to scale globally.

companies.name: AgBiome
companies.what: Genesis platform screens environmental microbes to discover biocontrol agents; lead product Howler is a microbial fungicide for soil-borne and foliar diseases.
companies.signal: Raised ~$233M total including a $116M Series D (Blue Horizon, Novalis; with Bayer, Mosaic, ARCH); broad microbial discovery library.

companies.name: Koppert
companies.what: Global biocontrol major supplying beneficial insects, microbials and pheromones; partnering with innovators (e.g. Provivi in Brazil) to distribute next-gen biocontrol.
companies.signal: Long-established global leader in biological crop protection with deep grower distribution; active commercialization partner in 2025 deals.

companies.name: Bayer Crop Science
companies.what: Major agrochem developing RNAi-based crop protection (sprayable and trait-based) and a biologicals portfolio; partners with Ginkgo and others on the technology.
companies.signal: Active RNAi and biologicals R&D programs; positions precision biologicals as part of its crop-protection pipeline and Ginkgo alliance.

companies.name: Andermatt Group
companies.what: Swiss biocontrol specialist (baculoviruses, microbials, biostimulants) expanding in emerging markets; regional partner for novel pheromone and RNAi products.
companies.signal: Named a 2025 East Africa partner in Provivi's pheromone rollout; established global biocontrol manufacturer and distributor.

variations.name: Recovered / circular nutrients (struvite, nutrient recapture)
variations.description: Wastewater treatment plants, manure digesters and food/biomass waste streams are mined to precipitate struvite (magnesium-ammonium-phosphate) and recover nitrogen and phosphorus as slow-release fertilizer, closing the nutrient loop and displacing energy-intensive mined phosphate and Haber-Bosch nitrogen.
variations.white_space: Recovery only captures a slice of nutrients (Ostara cites ~45-50% of inflow P) and depends on host wastewater/digester economics, so it is a complement, not a replacement, for mined/synthetic supply. Pure-play bio-based fertilizer makers that tried to scale on waste upcycling (Anuvia) failed on cost. Opening: tighter integration with utilities' phosphorus-discharge compliance needs and manure/agri-waste streams where disposal cost subsidizes the fertilizer.

companies.name: Ostara
companies.what: Pearl reactor precipitates struvite from municipal wastewater (with WASSTRIP enhancement) into Crystal Green, a root-activated slow-release P fertilizer.
companies.signal: WASSTRIP/Crystal Green operating at ~12 wastewater plants worldwide, recovering ~45-50% of inflow phosphorus; partnered with Evoqua for sales/delivery.

companies.name: NuReSys
companies.what: Belgian controlled struvite-crystallization technology recovering P (and N) from digested sludge and agro-industrial wastewater into pelletized Bio-Stru fertilizer.
companies.signal: 9 operational units across Europe on municipal sludge and agro-industrial streams; positioned as a major phosphorus-recovery technology provider.

companies.name: CNP (Centrisys/CNP)
companies.what: Provides AirPrex and related struvite-recovery/biosolids systems that precipitate struvite to improve sludge dewaterability and recover phosphorus as fertilizer.
companies.signal: Named among the leading struvite-recovery technology providers; commercial installations at wastewater resource-recovery facilities.

companies.name: Multiform Harvest
companies.what: Cone-reactor struvite recovery process designed for smaller/medium wastewater plants, recovering phosphorus and ammonia as fertilizer.
companies.signal: Cited among key struvite recovery companies; technology deployed alongside Ostara/WASSTRIP in utility projects.

companies.name: Fyto
companies.what: Grows duckweed in nitrogen-rich dairy wastewater; harvested biomass becomes cattle feed or is converted into plant-based fertilizer, recapturing manure nutrients.
companies.signal: Granted a fertilizer license; promising early trial results; plans to begin selling plant-based fertilizer products (2025).

companies.name: Anuvia Plant Nutrients
companies.what: Made SymTRX bio-based enhanced-efficiency fertilizer by upcycling recycled organic waste into a nutrient-dense granule at a repurposed Mosaic phosphate site.
companies.signal: Raised ~$307M (incl. $65.5M Series D, 2022) but suspended operations and liquidated assets effective May 2023 — a marquee failure on cost/scale.
